name: Brazilian tan / spray tan to even skin

lead: A spray tan applies a DHA solution to even out skin tone and give a bronzed look without UV exposure. The color shows within hours, and people use it before events, shoots and competitions.

DHA reacts with amino acids in the dead outer layer of skin to produce a brown color rather than acting as a dye. A 2005 review described DHA as the only sunless tanning ingredient approved by the FDA and spray-on products as delivering the formulation evenly for a full-body tan.

paras: The solution is sprayed across the body in a session, and the color develops over hours. It fades over about a week as the outer skin sheds, and people repeat it ahead of events.
The FDA approves DHA for external use only, not for inhalation or mucous membranes. Contact dermatitis and inhalation concerns are reported, and the tan does not protect against UV.

angle.text: A DHA spray tan reacts with the outer skin to give an even bronze color that lasts about a week, with no UV exposure. The color is visible within hours and is used before events, shoots and competitions.

lead: Spray tanning is a sunless tanning method in which a mist of dihydroxyacetone (DHA) solution is applied to the skin to produce a temporary bronze color. People use it to even out skin tone, add warmth to a pale complexion and give the face and body a healthy, defined look in photos or for events, without sun exposure. [1][2]

DHA is typically used at about 3 to 5 percent. It is not a dye: it reacts with amino acids in the dead outer layer of skin, producing color without melanin or ultraviolet light, and the color fades over roughly 3 to 10 days as skin sheds. [2] Application can be by hand-held airbrush from a technician, in an automated booth (widespread from the late 1990s), or with home spray and aerosol products. [1][2]
A 2005 review in Aesthetic Surgery Journal described spray-on tanning as delivering the formulation evenly to give a full-body tan without ultraviolet exposure. [1]
infobox: Airbrush by technician, booth, home spray [2]
DHA approved for external use; not eyes, lips, mucous membranes or inhalation [2]

paras: DHA reacts with amino acids in the outermost, dead layer of skin, producing brown compounds, with color developing over hours and fading as that layer sheds. Erythrulose, a co-ingredient in some formulas, works similarly but develops more slowly. [2]
Bronzers, which are cosmetics that wash off, differ from DHA tanners; Wikipedia notes that bronzers can look orangey or splotchy if misapplied and may transfer onto clothing. [2]

Wikipedia credits Eva Wittgenstein with noticing, at Cincinnati Children's Hospital in the 1950s, that oral DHA stained the skin brown. Man-Tan, the first commercial DHA self-tanner, appeared in 1959 and Coppertone's QT followed in 1960. Both gave orange-toned results that hurt the category's reputation, and later reformulations and spray booths broadened the market. [2]

The FDA approves DHA for external use only and not for the eyes, lips, mucous membranes or inhalation, and Wikipedia notes that spray booths can make those exposures hard to avoid. The FDA regulates DHA as a color additive. [2]

A DHA tan provides no UV protection of its own, and Wikipedia advises protection from the sun for about 24 hours after application. A 2007 study led by Katinka Jung reported more free radicals in DHA-treated skin exposed to UV, and a 2004 study from Bispebjerg Hospital reported DNA damage in cultured cells. A 2010 European Commission opinion found no risk, a conclusion critics say relied mostly on unpublished industry-linked studies. Fragrances, parabens and DHA itself can cause contact dermatitis in some people. [2]
No studies found examining spray tans specifically for evening skin tone. A 2005 review described spray-on tanning technology and formulations. [1]

lore.intro: Spray tans come up on looksmax.org mainly as a question about whether they are safer for skin quality than sun tanning.

claims.claim: Spray tans are a better alternative to sun tanning for skin health and looking young
